line: e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 Be2 Nb6 d3 Nc6 d4 d6
teaches: This whole defence provokes the centre forward in order to hit it, and the strike itself is not a subtle move — do not overthink it. The pawn challenges the advanced pawn, claims a share of the centre, and opens the bishop's diagonal, all in one routine gesture. Some moves are just correct.
explains: The pawn on d6 attacks the pawn on e5, the one the opening's early moves lured forward. However the tension resolves, the bishop behind the pawn gets its diagonal and the centre stops belonging to one side.

line: e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 Be2 Nb6 d3 Nc6 d4 d6 Nf3 dxe5 dxe5 Qxd1+
teaches: An open d-file with the enemy king still in the centre makes the queen trade a gaining move, not a drawish one: the recapture costs them castling or ties a piece to the back rank, and your development continues against a king that has to walk. Endgames where only one king is safe are middlegames in disguise.
explains: The queen takes on d1 with check, so the reply is forced and the trade happens on your terms — the recapturing piece is pulled to d1 and the king behind it has lost its castling future. The game heads toward an ending where one king already has a job and the other still needs one.
